topic: Bavoil HBAO tangent-horizon angle bias vs low-poly Phong normal facet acne rig
topic_zh: Bavoil HBAO 切平面仰角偏置对比朴素无偏置 SSAO 低模平滑法线棱线黑斑
scope: Deterministic Louis Bavoil, Miguel Sainz & Rouslan Dimitrov (SIGGRAPH 2008 NVIDIA HBAO) algebraic sine-bias horizon gating (AO = max(0, (sin(phi) - sin(theta_bias))/(1 - sin(theta_bias)))) versus naive unbiased horizon SSAO (AO = sin(phi)) and 64-ray elevation-cone inverse-trigonometric quadrature across 17 Phong normal interpolation stations (phi in [0.0 deg, 24.0 deg]). No neural AO inpainting execution.

protocol.function: V_HBAO(φ) = 1 − max(0, (sin φ − sin θ_bias) / (1 − sin θ_bias)) → Station-16 (φ=24°) V = 1.0000 (0.0000 Facet Acne)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 Phong normal tilt stations eliminate false low-poly facet self-occlusion stripes

good_fit: Horizon-Based Ambient Occlusion (HBAO / HBAO+ / GTAO) on low- and mid-poly smooth-shaded characters, vehicles, and props
Eliminating dark polygon-edge zebra stripes caused by Phong-interpolated normals tilting away from flat depth-buffer triangles
Evaluating sin(θ_h) − sin(θ_bias) algebraically via dot(H, N_smooth) without calling asin() or acos()
Combining with Jiménez GTAO cosine weighting (Round 81) and cross-bilateral normal-stopping filters (Round 95)
not_for: True geometric crevices deeper than θ_bias = 25°–30° (which pass the bias gate and receive physical ambient occlusion)
Flat-shadedfaceted meshes where the G-Buffer normal is identical to the geometric face normal (φ ≡ 0°)
